title: SRE weekly ops sync & reliability review — notes (2026-03-09, draft)
content:
Purpose / quick context:
- Prep notes for weekly SRE ops sync (Mon 10:00 PT). Focus: SLO health, paging trends last 7 days, top incidents, and action items for reliability improvements. Draft agenda below.

Attendees (invite):
- eng-sre oncall, eng-sre leads (Marcus, Priya), serving-runtime rep (Diego), infra (Shreya), product-observability (Maya), solutions-eng if needed.

Agenda (proposed, 30–40m):
1) Quick SLO snapshot (5m) — current status and error budget burn
2) Paging trends + noise analysis (8–10m)
3) Top incidents recap (10m)
4) Active reliability work / rollouts + risk review (5m)
5) Action items & owners (5m)

SLO snapshot (numbers are last 7d unless noted):
- API availability SLO (99.95% monthly target) — 7d observed: 99.91% (proj. monthly trend: ~99.88%) => small negative burn.
- Latency SLO (p50/p95 for softmax generation endpoint) — p50: 92ms (ok), p95: 480ms (target p95 < 400ms) => p95 over threshold.
- Embeddings endpoint SLO — 99.98% (good).
- Error budget remaining (calendar month): ~62% but current weekly burn rate projects ~30% budget consumption if current trend continues.
Notes:
- Latency p95 increase correlates with a spike in 1) long-sequence requests from a single customer test cluster and 2) CPU throttling on a subset of older nodes. Need to confirm contribution split.

Paging trends (last 7 days):
- Total pages: 38 (vs baseline 22) — significant increase.
- Top page sources: 1) model-runtime OOMs (12 pages), 2) transient downstream auth errors (8 pages), 3) high tail latency alerts (10 pages), 4) infra host flaps (8 pages).
- Time-of-day: majority of pages between 09:00–14:00 PT (matches customer workload window).

Noise analysis / quick hypotheses:
- OOM pages: concentrated on inference pools running quantized large models (q4) with sequence lengths > 4k. Likely cache/KV usage + unexpected prompt inflation causing memory spikes.
- Auth errors: temporary token validation failures linked to an internal cache for short-lived tokens — TTL misalignment after deploy on 2026-03-05.
- Host flaps: older kernel + NIC driver combo on g5dn-equivalent hosts; infra replaced 3 hosts but still seeing 1-2 residual flaps.

Top incidents (recent, brief summaries):
- INC-4582: model-runtime OOM cascade (2026-03-07 11:12–11:42 PT) — impact: degraded throughput for dedicated pools (customers A, C). Root cause: edge-case prompting + small memory leak in kv-cache path on runtime v1.9.1. Mitigation: hotfix v1.9.2 deployed 11:30 (evicted some caches, added guardrails). Postmortem in progress.
- INC-4557: auth-token cache TTL mismatch (2026-03-05 08:50–09:20 PT) — impact: 5–10% of API calls returned 401s intermittently for ~40m. Root cause: deploy that changed TTL default; cache-stale nodes kept old TTL. Rollback + coordinated cache invalidation fixed it. Action: change deploy checklist to include TTL sync step.
- INC-4520: infra host NIC driver bug (2026-03-03 intermittent) — flapping caused ~3% request retries. Infra replaced 3 hosts; monitoring still flagged one suspect.

Action items (concrete, owners, tentative due dates):
- AVA-1: Run mem-profiling sweep on runtime kv-cache code path to confirm leak hypothesis; add unit test for large-sequence behavior. Owner: Ava Martinez. Due: 2026-03-16.
- MARCUS-1: Add a guardrail in autoscaler to detect per-request sequence length spikes and throttle large requests into a separate pool or rate-limit. Owner: Marcus Lee. Due: 2026-03-23.
- PRIYA-1: Update deploy checklist and CI gate to ensure cache TTLs are validated pre-merge; add smoke test for token validation after deploy. Owner: Priya Nair. Due: 2026-03-12.
- DIEGO-1: Coordinate with infra to replace remaining suspect hosts and validate NIC driver firmware across fleets. Owner: Diego Alvarez + Infra. Due: 2026-03-13.
- SRE-OPS: Short-term: temporary webhook to aggregate model-long-sequence metrics into a dashboard and alert if inflight memory per-pool > 80%. Owner: oncall rotation (triage owner). Due: 2026-03-11.

Follow-ups / monitoring changes to propose in sync:
- Create a dashboard slice for sequence-length distribution (per-customer) and set alert thresholds for median & p95 sequence length.
- Add a derived metric: "kv-cache memory delta per-request" to detect growth pattern.
- Suppress / tune low-signal pages (infra flaps are noisy) — propose new PD escalation policy: infra-host-flap -> infra-ticket auto-create, but only PD page if >3 hosts affected or >10% traffic impacted.

Open questions / TODOs to discuss in meeting:
- Do we want to throttle long-sequence requests by default or move them to a separate heavy-pool? tradeoffs: latency impact for small requests vs protection for overall pool.
- For dedicated customers hitting long sequences (customer A test cluster): ask solutions-eng to coordinate a customer-level mitigation (quota/rate-limit) or encourage model truncation. Who owns customer communication? (Solutions-eng?).
- Is the p95 latency regression attributable more to model runtime or to network jitter from infra host flaps? Need A/B isolations.

Notes to self (meeting talking points):
- Start with SLO numbers + why p95 matters for tail-sensitive features. Keep it concrete: cite INC-4582 as example of cascade.
- Ask infra to commit to H/W replacements schedule and if any rolling reboots planned that could affect next week.
- Emphasize short-term mitigations (hotfix + alerts) vs longer-term design changes (separate heavy pools + autoscaler rules).

Draft message for post-sync summary (to send to #sre-ops):
"Quick update from today's ops sync: SLOs slightly under pressure due to a mix of runtime OOMs (kv-cache behavior with long sequences), auth TTL mismatch earlier this week, and a small number of infra host flaps. Action items assigned: mem-profiling + guardrails + deploy checklist improvements + infra host replacements. Expect a follow-up next week with progress on the mem-profiling and autoscaler guardrail work. See linked artifacts for incident details: CONFLUENCE-RI-2026-weekly, JIRA-RI-9876."

Meeting logistics / prep for me:
- Bring timeline for INC-4582 and quick diff of hotfix (v1.9.1 -> v1.9.2).
- Have charts ready: p95 latency trend (7d), pages per day (30d), sequence-length histogram (sample last 72h).
- Ask Marcus to walk through autoscaler proposal (5m).

End notes / backlog items to consider later:
- Consider runbook updates: add step to clear the token cache after TTL-affecting deploys.
- Longer-term: investigate per-customer memory isolation in dedicated pools (cgroups / container memory limits) vs per-request throttling.
- Align with product on acceptable latency SLOs for heavy-sequence workloads (maybe separate SLO tiers?).

Last edited quick log: 2026-03-09 08:45 PT — added INC-4582 summary, updated action owners.

---
This is a working doc; expect edits during and after the sync. Keep as users scratchpad + source for the post-sync note.
